rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community that reserves worship and appeal to God reflects a delegated divine trust and receives a share in creation; this supports communal consensus as a legally probative source.
rows.anchor: ümmetin icmâ‘ında da bir delâlet-i teşrî‘iye mevcut olabileceğini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relation between the basmala and Fatiha unfolds the primordial covenant between the eternal Lord and creation, inscribing a relation already present in human nature.
rows.anchor: besmele ile Fâtiha arasındaki sibâk-ı tenâsübün rûhu ezel ile lâyezâl beynindeki bu mu‘âdele nisbetinin inkişâfıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatiha proceeds as instruction; the command to read in the name of the Lord is a key contextual sign of this teaching purpose.
rows.anchor: Fâtiha’nın bizzat kendisindeki sevki bir sevk-i ta’lîmdir

rows.speaker: bazı müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some exegetes posit an implicit command meaning say this at the start of Fatiha.
rows.anchor: bazı müfessirîn başta “böyle söyle” mealinde قل emrinin mukadder olduğunu

rows.speaker: muhakkıkīn
rows.claim: The discerning exegetes hold that the teaching is clear from the style itself, without supplying an omitted command.
rows.anchor: muhakkıkīn bu takdîre hâcet kalmaksızın sâde, siyâk-ı üslûbun bu ta‘lîmi iş‘âra kâfi olduğunda musırdırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening three verses speak about God in the unseen; reflection makes God present to the worshipper, who can then turn to direct address and pledge worship and need.
rows.anchor: ma‘rifetullâha müte‘allik olan üç âyet tamâmen gāibâne

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from unseen narration to direct address is an eloquent turn of address that compresses extensive meanings and contributes to the Qur’an’s inimitability.
rows.anchor: bir üslûb-i iltifâtın böyle tam makamında ve birçok cümlelere muhtaç mazmunları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatiha’s successive clauses unfold the opening praise and return to alhamdu lillah; the surah is the root and comprehensive representative of the other Qur’anic surahs.
rows.anchor: Diğer süver-i Kur’an ile münasebâtı ise, Fâtiha; “Ümmü’l-Kur’ân”, “Ümmü’l-Kitâb”, “Esâs” isimlerinin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala is the crown, the Qur’an a perfect body, Fatiha its head, and alhamdu lillah its face; mercy, guidance, worship, and divine unity express its spiritual life.
rows.anchor: besmele bir taç, Kur’an bir vücûd-i ekmel, Fâtiha onun başı, ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ bu baştaki sîmâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd is beautiful verbal praise that honors an agent for a voluntary benefaction or its source, goodness; it combines aspects of praise and gratitude and lacks a single Turkish equivalent.
rows.anchor: Hamd, ihtiyârî bir ihsâna veya onun mebde’i olan bir hüsne karşı inşirah ile sâhibine tâzim ifade eden bir zikr-i cemîldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medh can praise living or inanimate things and can precede or follow a favor; hamd is directed to a choosing benefactor after a favor, though the benefit need not reach the praiser.
rows.anchor: medh, hayatı ve ihtiyârı olana da olmayana da yapılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shukr responds in speech, action, or heart to a blessing actually received; spoken gratitude is also hamd and medh, while inward or bodily thanks need not be either.
rows.anchor: Şükürde ise bu da şarttır. Zira şükür gelmiş olan bir nimete kavlen veya fiilen veya kalben mün‘imini tâzim ile mukabele etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every hamd is medh but not every medh is hamd; hamd is broader than gratitude in one respect and narrower in another, and unlike empty flattery both hamd and shukr affirm truth.
rows.anchor: Her hamd medhdir, lâkin her medh hamd değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd springs from justified hope or experienced enjoyment and leans toward the future, whereas shukr celebrates an accomplished gift and its received fulfillment.
rows.anchor: Hamd delile müstenid haklı bir ümidin neşvesiyle veyahut şükür gibi tahakkuk etmiş bir tenâ‘‘umun

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: The Prophet commands that dust be thrown in the faces of professional eulogists, illustrating the moral danger of medh that can become flattery.
rows.anchor: Aleyhi’s-salâtü ve’s-selâm Efendimiz “Meddahların yüzlerine toprak saçınız

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: The Prophet says that one who does not praise people does not praise God, making hamd generally commendable.
rows.anchor: Nâsa hamd etmeyen Allah’a da hamd etmez: مَنْ لَمْ يَحْمَدِ النَّاسَ لَمْ يَحْمَدِ اللّٰهَّٰ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude is a distinctive mark of people of truth, yet only a few servants attain it.
rows.anchor: Şükür ise böyle erbâb-ı hakīkatin şi‘ârı olduğundan

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ömeru’l-Fârûk
rows.claim: Umar’s remark that truth left him no friend conveys how difficult it is to remain faithful to truth.
rows.anchor: Nitekim fânî fi’l-hak olan Hazret-i Ömeru’l-Fârûk

rows.speaker: Gustave Le Bon
rows.claim: Le Bon and other thinkers conclude that imagination rules people more strongly than reality.
rows.anchor: Bunu mülâhaza eden bazı mütefekkirîn, ezcümle zamanımızda Fransız Gustave Le Bon

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects Le Bon’s conclusion: imagination affects people because it can represent reality, so reality remains the true source of its force.
rows.anchor: Fakat bu doğru değildir. Çünkü hayalde görülen o hâkimiyet hakikati temsil edebilmesi haysiyetindendir

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: The Prophet calls hamd the head of gratitude and says that whoever fails to praise God has not thanked Him.
rows.anchor: olmasını iktizâ eder. Fi’l-vâki‘Resûl-i Ekrem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verbal expressions of reverence count as hamd; announcing a blessing is a moral virtue that praises its free agent and rightly rejoices in the happiness received.
rows.anchor: tahdîs-i nimet bir gurûr-ı temeddüh değil, nankörlüğü silen büyük bir fazilettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human happiness depends on recognizing and tasting a blessing, not merely possessing it; the recipient’s expressed hamd lets the giver witness that the gift reached its fitting recipient.
rows.anchor: saadet tena‘‘umun kendisinde ve kemmiyetinde değil keyfiyetinde, yani zevki takdir edilip hissedilmesindedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving stands above receiving, so the station of the praised giver is the highest rank; the joy of this rank culminates in further hamd and increased gifts.
rows.anchor: makām-ı in‘âm, makām-ı tena‘‘umun fevkindedir. Binâen‘aleyh Makām-ı Mahmûdiyet ekmel-i merâtib ve aksâ-yı metâlibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd advances through four ranks: praising, being praised, uniting both, then receiving praise while praising.
rows.anchor: 1. Hâmidiyet, 2. Mahmûdiyet, 3. Hâmidiyet ve Mahmûdiyet, 4. Mahmûdiyet ve Hâmidiyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final rank manifests the divine names Hamid, Mahmud, and Hamid together; the Prophet also bears the related names Ahmed and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: mahmûdiyet ve hâmidiyeti cem‘eden Hamîd, Mahmûd, Hâmid esmâ-i hüsnâsının tecellîsini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised station of praise belongs especially to the Seal of the Prophets and is the station of the great intercession, where he receives the banner of praise.
rows.anchor: Makām-ı Mahmûd bilhassa Hâtemü’l-Enbiyâ Efendimiz’e mev‘ud olan ve onu hâmidiyetten mahmûdiyete terakki ettiren bir makām-ı a‘lâdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through the Prophet’s intercession, the community gathered beneath the banner of praise shares in divine hamd, and the people of Paradise conclude their plea with this verse.
rows.anchor: ehl-i cennetin davalarının sonu da ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ olacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd’s fullest nature speaks through the Prophet’s Ahmediyyah and Muhammadiyyah; its ultimate reality belongs at its beginning and end to God alone.
rows.anchor: lafzen ve mânen mâhiyet-i hamd, bir Hakīkat-i Muhammediye’dir. Ve bu hakikatin evvel ve âhir Allah teâlâ’ya ihtisâsı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in alhamd can express a known instance, totality, kind, or essence; because no particular hamd is presupposed, it here gathers the entire genus and all its ranks.
rows.anchor: Lisân-ı Arab’da ال ‘ahd-i ferd veya ‘ahd-i istiğrak veya ‘ahd-i cins ve hakikat ifade eden bir harf-i ta‘rîftir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in lillah denotes entitlement, particularity, and ownership; the whole genus and every form of hamd belongs to God.
rows.anchor: للّٰهّٰ da lâm, ihtisas, istihkak, milk mânalarında zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alhamdu lillah informs believers, implies reverent praise, and uses a timeless nominal sentence; the four following clauses explain it, making Fatiha one sentence in substance.
rows.anchor: Fâtiha, bu tek cümle-i ismiyeden ibaret bir kelâmdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound plural al-alamin foregrounds rational beings; a concise Turkish rendering is difficult, but it means God alone is Lord of all realms and especially their rational inhabitants.
rows.anchor: Kur’an “Rabbu’l-‘avâlim” demiyor da “Rabbü’l-âlemîn” diyor ve bununla bilhassa zevi’l-‘ukūlü tağlib ederek onların nazar-ı dikkatini celb eyliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural’s focus on rational consciousness, reinforced by the merciful and sovereign attributes, draws reason from unseen knowledge to witnessed presence and the direct covenant of worship.
rows.anchor: şu‘ûr-i ‘ukalâyı gāibden şuhûda getirip إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ diye hitab ile ‘arz-ı tevhîd u mîsâka sevk edecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rab is a verbal noun for nurturing, applied emphatically to the nurturer; rububiyyah names this relation.
rows.anchor: “Rab” aslında terbiye mânasına bir masdar olduğu hâlde mübalağa kasdıyla mürebbîye ıtlak edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rab entails complete power to nurture, govern, guide, command, reward, and discipline, and also means owner; without a qualifying relation it is reserved for God.
rows.anchor: sâde mâlik veya sâde terbiye mefhumları değil, ikisine de bütün levâzımıyla sâhip olan bir kādir-i kayyûm anlaşılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nurturing is gradual movement toward perfection, visibly at work throughout the universe; contemplating the realms reveals the law of divine nurturing, while the realms themselves are known through their relation to God.
rows.anchor: Âlemînin her kısmında ise terbiye ve tekâmül kanunlarının cereyânı her an ve her lahza meşhuddur

rows.speaker: bir kısım felâsife
rows.claim: Some philosophers say the whole cosmos came to be all at once, with or without causes, rather than through gradual development.
rows.anchor: bunlardan bir kısmı hepsinin def‘î olarak sebepli veya sebepsiz birdenbire tekevvün etmiş bulunduğunu

rows.speaker: bir kısım felâsife
rows.claim: Another group denies origination by claiming that the present cosmic order has existed eternally; on this view there is no real progress, striving, or acquisition.
rows.anchor: tabiat davasıyla tekevvünü inkâr edercesine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daily observation and inference show that things arise gradually and disappear gradually; examples from geology, plants, animals, and human development contradict those denials.
rows.anchor: efrâd-ı eşyânın, dün yok iken ufacıktan hudûsa gelip tedrîcen büyüdüğünü ve bilakis yine tedrîcen kaybolup gittiğini her gün bi’t-tecribe görüyoruz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing stages of the cosmos and human life still disclose a continuous, powerful reality that binds them and gives the observer awareness of unity.
rows.anchor: bütün bu cereyanları izhar ve rabt ederek bize dâima vahdet şuurunu veren kādir-i kayyûm bir hakikat her dem, her lahza i‘lân-ı vücûd ediyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign in al-alamin, later clarified by al-Baqara’s description of the Qur’an as guidance for the Godfearing, signals the wisdom of revelation.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Bakara’nın başında هُدًۭى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ nazm-ı celîlinde tebeyyün edecek olan bu işâret-i mücmele

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Observation, experience, and reason jointly establish origination and development; science may affirm evolution, but it must recognize God as its complete first cause.
rows.anchor: Âlemde halk, terbiye, ıstıfâ ve tekâmül bir sünnet-i câriye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some misuse evolutionary language by treating nature’s law as an uncaused absolute, displacing divine nurturing and making humanity the absolute summit of existence.
rows.anchor: bunlar bu tekâmülü Hak teâlâ’nın bir eser-i terbiyesi telakkī etmeyip, müessirsiz, illetsiz olarak tabiatta bizzat cârî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Science depends on causality: what comes into existence after not existing must have a cause, since nothing can arise from nothing.
rows.anchor: yok iken var olabilenin her hâlde bir sebebi vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cause and effect must be proportionate: an effect cannot exceed its complete cause, and known effects disclose their cause; otherwise nonbeing would produce being.
rows.anchor: ma‘lûlât ne kadar çok olursa olsun mecmû‘u illetin kudretini tecavüz edemezler, onunla mütenâsib olurlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Consciousness, knowledge, and reason cannot have a blind force or blind nature as their complete cause; natural laws require an intelligent necessary being.
rows.anchor: Hâdisâtta şuur, ilim, akıl gibi ma‘lûlât meşhud olup dururken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wheat seed’s multiplication illustrates that one cannot explain the many grains by the seed’s isolated capacity alone; each added stage receives perfection from beyond itself.
rows.anchor: bir buğday danesi toprağa düşer ve şerâitini bulunca biter, açılır, büyür, sümbüllenir, nihâyet bir başakta yüz buğday tanesi verebilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The law of development therefore describes educative growth supplied from beyond each stage, not self-sufficient natural evolution; what is deficient cannot produce the complete on its own.
rows.anchor: gelen bir kemâl vardır. Bu ise tekâmül-i tabî‘î değil, tekâmül-i terbiyevîdir

rows.speaker: Spencer
rows.claim: Even Spencer, treated as a leading formulator of natural evolution, says an Absolute must exist beyond finite natural development, though human knowledge cannot encompass it.
rows.anchor: feylesof Spencer[^60] bile bunun için mutlakın vücûdu zarûrî olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny divine nurturing contradict themselves by investing effort in education and child-rearing, which presuppose that development can be guided.
rows.anchor: bunlar kendi kanâ‘at-i ameliyelerinde bu nazariyelerini her gün, her lahza cerh ve nakz eyliyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge begins from a single unpartnered Truth and tests every conclusion by relating it to that highest Truth; without this relation, nature and evolution cannot be affirmed as real.
rows.anchor: ilim her şeyden evvel hiç şerîki olmayan bir Hak tanır ve dâima vahdet mikyâsıyla yürür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absolute knowledge is God’s eternal knowledge and self-disclosure; human knowledge is only a relative, contingent disclosure of that truth.
rows.anchor: İlm-i mutlak zât-ı Hakk’ın kendine tecellîsi ve O’nun ilm-i kadîmidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without God’s perfect lordship and nurturing, neither existence nor development could be real; the world’s real share in these qualities reveals God as Lord of all realms.
rows.anchor: Âlem ve biz böyle değilsek bir hisse-i vücûdumuz, bir hisse-i kemâlimiz, bir hisse-i terbiyemiz, hakkiyet isnad edilecek bir izâfetle bize tecellî ediyorsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world is the collection of all things other than God that point to Him through causal relations; any part possessing an ordered relation can be called a realm.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın mâsivâsı olup illiyet alâkasıyla Allah’a delâlet eden eşyânın mecmû‘u ve bir nizâm-ı ictimâ‘îyi hâiz bulunan her kısmı âlem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alam derives from the idea of a means of knowledge and is a collective noun; it is not applied to a wholly isolated individual.
rows.anchor: مَا يُعْلَمُ بِهِ yani vesîle-i ilim mefhûmunu ifade eden “âlem” kelimesi “alem”, “alâmet” maddesinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound rational plural and the definite article extend the meaning across all realms and foreground rational beings; understanding the Lord of the worlds requires conceiving rational agents.
rows.anchor: cem‘-i âkil getirilmesi de ukalâ kısmının tağlîbine delâlet eyler ve ukalâyı tasavvur etmeden Rabbü’l-âlemîn iyi idrak olunamayacağını ifham eyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True knowledge is not mere conception but assent to the real relation between what is conceived; the ordered events we perceive become signs through this truth-consciousness.
rows.anchor: Asıl ilim ise tasavvur değil tasdîk-i haktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every ordered community of things, from inner awareness to external objects, is named a realm because it serves as a sign and means of knowing God’s creation, lordship, and perfection.
rows.anchor: her cemâ‘at-i eşyâ ve bütün cemâ‘ât-i eşyâ Hak teâlâ’ya

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those who truly witness, nothing is seen without God also being seen behind, before, or with it; the world is other-than-God and God lies beyond it.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i şuhûd için âlemde bir şey yoktur ki görülsün de arkasında ondan evvel veya ondan sonra, onunla beraber Allah teâlâ görülmesin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs of God’s unity may be immediate or detailed, sensory or imagined, and can be read through perception, memory, and reason; all require conscious attention.
rows.anchor: Bu delâlet de mücmel, mufassal ve her biri şuhûdî, hayâlî olmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We know things through conscious attention and the representations it produces, yet we also judge external entities to possess objective reality beyond those representations.
rows.anchor: biz eşyâyı şuurlarımızın ta‘allukuyla şuhûden ve bu ta‘alluktan hâsıl olan suretlerle, hatıralarla tasavvuren ve aklen tanırız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judging the self, consciousness, and external objects as truly corresponding already presupposes an encompassing necessary truth that guarantees their relations; this tacit attribution to God grounds our judgments.
rows.anchor: ben bütün bunlardan evvel ve bütün bunların mâverâsında, önünde sonunda, beraberinde enfüsî ve âfâkī emkine ve ezmânı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul cannot itself be the ultimate cause of all truth: it acknowledges its limitations and does not claim to create at will or to have existed eternally.
rows.anchor: ben öyle olsaydım her istediğimi yapar ve sana ezelden beri hiçbir yokluk göstermezdim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the basic judgment I exist depends on affirming a true relation between self-awareness and being, which rests on God’s encompassing truth; all limited knowledge is thereby God’s gift.
rows.anchor: ben kendimi duyarken, önümden, sonumdan, zâhirimden, bâtınımdan muhît olan hakkı ve izâfet-i hakkı beraberimde olarak tasdik etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The certainty I exist requires consciousness, and the truth of that self-awareness is guaranteed by the necessary testimony of the sovereign God, the beginning and end of every certainty.
rows.anchor: Bu da Vâcibu’l-vücûd, hâkim-i mutlak bir Zât-ı Hakk’ın zarûrî bir tasdîkiyle, şehâdetiyle bedîhîdir

rows.speaker: bazıları; bazıları
rows.claim: Some call the Creator’s existence self-evident in a clear way, others self-evident but hidden, and others demonstrative; its appearance depends on each person’s strength of self-awareness.
rows.anchor: bazıları vücûd-i Bârî’ye bedîhî-i celî, bazıları bedîhî-i hafî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world is a sign of God, while God is its witness and light; the cited verses describe Him as the light of heaven and earth, witness over all, and first and last.
rows.anchor: âlem O’nun delili iken O da âlemin şâhidi, nûrudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is assent to this light, and Islam is living out that assent and relation to God.
rows.anchor: İman bu nûra iz‘ân, dîn-i İslâm da bu iz‘ânı, bu izâfeti yaşamaktır
